title: Evening Run
headline: Short brick run off the bike — cadence held steady and effort stayed easy.
analysis: Just over a mile in 10.2 minutes (about 10:04/mi) straight off the ROUVY ride, with cadence steady at 83 spm and heart rate topping out at 138 bpm. Relative effort was minimal at 9 — exactly what a short transition run should be.

title: ROUVY - IRONMAN Jacksonville (First 42km)
headline: Steady aerobic ride at controlled power — textbook base-building effort.
analysis: 87 minutes averaging 111w and 112 bpm — comfortably aerobic with a relative effort of just 28. Cadence sat lower than usual at 59 rpm, consistent with the course's terrain profile.

title: Morning Swim
headline: Solid long swim — nearly 3,000m with heart rate holding in a comfortable aerobic range.
analysis: 2,972m in just over 70 minutes, averaging 115 bpm and topping out at 129 — clearly aerobic, sustainable pacing for a swim of this length. The relative effort of 75 reflects the volume more than the intensity.

title: Evening Run
headline: Massive effort — your longest run of the build and by far the hardest, with heart rate climbing into the 180s–190s late.
analysis: 12 miles in 115 minutes (about 9:34/mi), with 3 new PRs set along the way. Heart rate built steadily through the walk/run intervals, peaking at 190 bpm in the back third — a relative effort of 327 makes this the single biggest session logged this build. Worth extra recovery attention given the spike.

title: Afternoon Ride
headline: Nearly 24 miles at an easy aerobic effort, with three new segment PRs along the way.
analysis: 88 minutes covering 23.9 miles, averaging 118 bpm (max 144) — solidly Zone 2. Relative effort was moderate at 57, and you picked up three bronze segment PRs without pushing outside the aerobic zone.

title: Evening Run
headline: Solid brick run off the bike — legs held up well at a steady aerobic effort.
analysis: 3.3 miles in just under 31 minutes (about 9:19/mi) directly after the ride, averaging 139 bpm. An effort score of 59 reflects a controlled, sustainable brick — exactly the kind of session that builds bike-to-run durability.

title: Morning Swim
headline: Easy recovery swim — heart rate stayed low the entire session.
analysis: 3,063m in just over 71 minutes with average heart rate at only 108 bpm (max 122) — a clearly easy, recovery-paced swim. The relative effort of 39 confirms this was about volume and technique, not intensity.

title: Evening Run
headline: Strong finish with real negative splits — you pushed into the anaerobic zone over the final two miles.
analysis: 4 miles negative-split from 10:26/mi down to 9:35/mi, with heart rate climbing into the 170s–190s bpm range over the back half. Relative effort of 108 and cadence holding steady at 82 spm — a well-executed progression run.

title: Lunch Ride
headline: Nearly 68 miles of aerobic endurance work with 50 PRs proves that steady Zone 2 discipline pays dividends
analysis: You held a remarkably consistent 124 bpm average across 4+ hours in the saddle, staying well below your 155 max even during those PR efforts. That massive 90-minute stretch around mile 39 shows serious mental fortitude, and your heart rate control through the final 8 miles (averaging 2:45-3:43 pace with HR in the 120s-130s) demonstrates you had plenty left in the tank. This is exactly the kind of controlled, high-volume session that builds the aerobic base triathletes need.

title: ROUVY - IRONMAN 70.3 HRADEC KRALOVE 2024
headline: Steady Zone 2 endurance builder through the IRONMAN 70.3 course, but that 54 rpm cadence is leaving watts on the table
analysis: You kept this controlled at 115 bpm average heart rate (maxing at just 133) over 2 hours—textbook aerobic base work. However, your 54 rpm average cadence is well below the efficient 85-95 range, which means you're grinding through those climbs like the 13.5-minute Nahořany segment rather than spinning smoothly. Focus on higher cadence drills in your next indoor session to develop that neuromuscular efficiency before race day.

title: Morning Run
headline: Short but steady effort with a strong finish at a faster-than-average pace
analysis: You covered 1.51 miles in 15:12, working at a controlled average pace of 10:04/mi that's actually quicker than your 30-day average of 9:43/mi. Your heart rate climbed steadily from 150 bpm in mile 1 to 154 bpm in the final 0.51 miles, showing good cardiovascular engagement throughout. That cadence of 82.7 spm is on the lower side—try to target 85-90 to improve efficiency and reduce ground contact time on future runs.

title: Evening Swim
headline: Solid 2,126-meter effort with controlled pacing and steady heart rate discipline
analysis: You held a consistent aerobic zone throughout this 48-minute session, keeping your average heart rate at 107 bpm with a max of just 117—excellent cardiovascular control for a moderate effort swim. Your first mile at 36:22 came in slightly faster than your 30-day average of 37:22/mi while maintaining a lower heart rate of 105 bpm, showing improved efficiency. The second mile segment saw your heart rate climb to 110 bpm as you worked through the final kilometers, reflecting good sustained effort without redlining.

title: Morning Run
headline: Heart rate climbed steadily through a progressively slower 3-miler, suggesting fatigue accumulation
analysis: Your pace degraded from 9:83 to 10:17 min/mi over the first three miles while your average heart rate climbed from 138 to 155 bpm—a classic sign of accumulating fatigue rather than a controlled effort. At 10:00/mi average, you ran 16 seconds per mile slower than your 30-day average of 9:44/mi, yet still logged a relative effort of 84. That cadence of 82 spm is quite low for running; working toward 85-90+ steps per minute could help you maintain pace more efficiently when fatigue sets in.
